description:
We are a group of B.Tech CSE students with an interest in AI/ML, data science, space technology, and solving real-world problems through technology. We enjoy exploring new ideas, working with data, and building innovative solutions. We've also worked on AI/ML-based projects involving anomaly detection and data analysis.

We are passionate about Python, AI/ML, web development, data visualization, GIS, astronomy, and enjoying brainstorming, experimenting, and building together.
summary:
ARES-OPS: Autonomous Regolith Evaluation & Surface Operations Planetary System

1. What It Does
ARES-OPS is an interactive Mars mission control and astronaut navigation platform set in Gale Crater. Features include 360° 3D Martian Street View, real-time ground-projected slope hazard heatmaps, 14m lookahead steep-slope alarms, autonomous A* hazard routing, 3D Mount Sharp altimetry, NASA JPL Mars Trek integration, and a live flight rules engine tracking metabolic oxygen and safe walkback reserves.

2. How It Works
This zero-install web app models 40 × 40 km of Gale Crater using MOLA elevation benchmarks and central-difference slope kernels. A* pathfinding with a binary MinHeap avoids slopes exceeding 15°, accounting for sand and bedrock impedance. A Martian physiology engine adapts Tobler’s hiking function to 0.38g gravity and spacesuit resistance, calculating oxygen burn and triggering abort warnings before reserves run critical.

3. Benefits & Vision
ARES-OPS reveals hidden micro-slopes and unstable scree to prevent traversal accidents, protect spacesuits from sharp boxwork ridges, and maximize scientific returns. Our vision is an open-source prototype for future astronaut HUDs on NASA's Artemis lunar and crewed Mars missions.

4. Tech Stack
HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+), Three.js (WebGL), Canvas 2D, Leaflet.js, Git.
details:
1. What Exactly Does It Do?
ARES-OPS (Autonomous Regolith Evaluation & Surface Operations Planetary System) is an integrated mission control and astronaut surface navigation platform. It provides:
• 3D Martian Street View: An interactive, ground-level 360-degree panoramic explorer that places the user in the boots of an astronaut traversing the floor and slopes of Gale Crater. Users can explore in first-person helmet view or third-person 3D spacesuit avatar mode.
• Dynamic Slope Hazard Heatmap: Projects color-coded incline grades directly onto the Martian regolith mesh in real time (Green: <10° safe; Amber: 10°-15° caution; Red: >15° NASA NO-GO hazard).
• Lookahead Steep Slope Alarm: Proactively samples ground gradients 14 meters ahead of the astronaut's active heading and fires a high-visibility master warning banner if an unsafe slope approaches.
• Autonomous A* Hazard Routing: Computes the "Best Safest Shortest Path" between science waypoints, strictly diverting routes around escarpments, cliffs, and loose sand traps.
• Real-Time NASA HRP Flight Rules Engine: Continuously tracks walking velocity, metabolic oxygen burn, and the critical Walkback Horizon (ensuring a 45-minute emergency oxygen reserve at Base Camp).
• Mount Sharp 3D Altimetry & Orbital DEM: Visualizes the entire 40 km × 40 km study quadrant with adjustable vertical relief (1.0x to 3.0x), MOLA height coloration, and a glowing 3D tubular route spline.
• Direct NASA JPL Mars Trek Integration: Deep-links directly to Gale Crater on NASA's official Solar System Treks portal.

2. How Does It Work?
The platform operates as a client-side, zero-install single page application built on standard web technologies:
• Elevation Modeling: Gale Crater topography is evaluated on a 40 km × 40 km domain utilizing analytical approximations fitted to MGS MOLA elevation benchmarks. Terrain gradients are computed using a spatial central-difference kernel:
gx = (h(x+s, y) - h(x-s, y)) / (2s)
gy = (h(x, y+s) - h(x, y-s)) / (2s)
Slope θ = arctan(sqrt(gx² + gy²)) * (180 / π)
• Pathfinding Engine: An A* search algorithm operating over a discrete cost grid uses a MinHeap priority queue. Any node exceeding a 15° slope is assigned infinite traversal cost (hard-pruned), while passable terrain is weighted by slope angle and surface impedance derived from 2001 Mars Odyssey THEMIS thermal inertia (loose aeolian drift sand vs. cohesive bedrock).
• Martian Physiology Engine: Astronaut walking speed is governed by a modified Tobler hiking function adapted for 0.38g gravity and pressurized spacesuit joint resistance (3.0 km/h on flat ground, 1.2 km/h on caution slopes, 0 km/h on >15° slopes). Metabolic air depletion is modeled dynamically:
C_air = (Distance / 1000) * R_base * [1 + 1.4 * (min(θ, 15°) / 15°)] * η
If remaining oxygen reaches the return cost plus the mandatory 45-minute reserve, the system triggers the MASTER ABORT EVA alarm.
• Visual Rendering: Built with Three.js (WebGL) for procedural ground mesh tessellation, sky dome scattering, and 3D astronaut rendering; and Leaflet.js in EPSG:4326 for GIS tile management.

3. What Benefits Does It Have?
• Prevents Fatal Traversal Incidents: Traditional 2D orbital maps cannot depict surface drop-offs or micro-slopes. ARES-OPS protects crew safety through real-time lookahead warnings and ground-projected heatmaps.
• Protects Spacesuit Integrity: Prevents punctures on razor-sharp boxwork hydrothermal vein ridges and slip accidents on unstable scree slopes.
• Maximizes Planetary Science Return: Enables astronauts to safely reach the primary geological objective—Mount Sharp's ancient boxwork formations—to sample ancient habitable hydrothermal environments.
• Zero-Friction Deployment: Runs out-of-the-box in any modern browser without installing Node.js, Python, or external software.

4. What Do We Hope to Achieve?
Our vision is to transform planetary surface EVA navigation from a reactive, high-risk endeavor into an intuitive, mathematically verified science. We hope to establish ARES-OPS as an open-source prototype that can be integrated into future astronaut heads-up displays (HUDs) for NASA's Artemis Lunar missions and the eventual crewed human missions to Mars.

5. Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, and Software
• Programming Languages: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+).
• 3D Graphics & Rendering: Three.js (WebGL), Canvas 2D API for real-time elevation profile scrubber and HUD telemetry minimap.
• GIS & Cartography: Leaflet.js (EPSG:4326 equirectangular planetary projection), OGC Web Map Tile Service (WMTS).
• Algorithms & Data Structures: A* Pathfinding with Binary MinHeap Priority Queue, Central Finite Difference Slope Gradient Kernels, Tobler Martian Hiking Function.
